ŏrīgĭnālis , e, adj. origo,
I.primitive, original (post-class.): “Ceres frugum parens originalis,” App. M. 11, p. 257 : “recurram ad originales libros,” Hier. in Gal. 3, 10 : “rerum species,” Macr. Somn. Scip. 1, 2 : coloni, Cod. Th. 11, 1, 14.—Hence, adv.: ŏrīgĭnālĭ-ter , originally (eccl. Lat.), Aug. Trin. 3, 9; id. Retract. 1, 15.
From A Latin Dictionary (Charlton T. Lewis, Charles Short, Oxford, Clarendon Press, 1879)
